_comment: Deployment configuration for the tagging kit. Everything the client must not hardcode in code lives here. Surface tagRelays in the app's Settings UI; the rest is instance identity.
_tagRelays: The tag-hub relay set. Reads query (tagRelays UNION the user's read relays); tag/tagging publishes go to (tagRelays UNION the user's write relays). dcosl.brainstorm.world is the hub the reference instances negentropy-sync through — the cold-start default, NOT a protocol requirement. Make this list user-editable in Settings.

houseInstance.name: tags.brainstorm.world
houseInstance._api: The REST API is same-origin (no CORS) — browsers CANNOT call it cross-origin. This kit is pure-relay; apiBase is documented only for server-side/proxy use and for re-fetching localTaPubkey below (GET /api/assistant/pubkey) when rotating config.

_localTaPubkey: The house instance's Tapestry Assistant pubkey — fetched from https://tags.brainstorm.world/api/assistant/pubkey (2026-07-23). Per-deployment: if you point the kit at a different instance, re-fetch and replace. This is deployment CONFIG, not code — never inline it as a literal in source.
_canonicalConceptPubkey: The LEGACY canonical namespace (Tapestry ADR-0015): the `tag` and `nostr-user-tag` concept handles are historically bound to this pubkey across ALL reference instances so pre-existing tags/taggings stay visible. Used ONLY to compose concept z-handles; never as an author filter or signer identity.
_zHandlePubkeys: [canonicalConceptPubkey, localTaPubkey] in that order — the namespace list passed as `taPubkeys`/`zHandlePubkeys` to every builder and as `honoredAuthorities` to every classifier. Canonical first: the event-tagging orchestrator prefers headers authored under zHandlePubkeys[0].

trust._comment: house-ta = build the asserter-trust predicate from the house's NIP-85 kind-30382 assertions (see sdk/trust.js). unknownPolicy 'trusted' counts asserters with no published score — matching the reference deployment's un-provisioned-POV fallback. 'everyone' mode skips 30382 lookups entirely.
